s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with radiation to the jaw and associated symptoms
salient_findings: Chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression on ECG
key_facts: Subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion 4 days prior to presentation
3 hours of substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously the day prior to presentation
Constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with radiation to the jaw and associated symptoms
salient_findings: Chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression on ECG
key_facts: Subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion 4 days prior to presentation
3 hours of substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously the day prior to presentation
Constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of chest pressure radiating to the jaw, diaphoresis, and vomiting, along with ECG findings of ST-segment elevations and PR-segment depression, and elevated inflammatory markers, are consistent with pericarditis. The normal coronary angiography and transthoracic echocardiogram also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Myopericarditis
rejected.why: While some findings could suggest myopericarditis, the normal cardiac examination and lack of significant left ventricular dysfunction make this less likely.

rejected.label: Myocarditis
rejected.why: The normal left ventricular end-diastolic pressure and transthoracic echocardiogram, along with the lack of significant cardiac examination abnormalities, make myocarditis less likely.

rejected.label: Tietze syndrome
rejected.why: Tietze syndrome typically presents with sharp, stabbing chest pain and swelling of the chest wall, which is not described in this patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: The normal coronary angiography and lack of significant cardiac examination abnormalities make acute myocardial infarction unlikely, despite the elevated troponin level, which can also be seen in pericarditis.
